blocks.text: HOARDING CLEANOUT FAQ
Hoarding Cleanouts in Richmond Hill — Honest Answers to Common Questions

items.q: What's the cost to clean out a hoarder's house in Richmond Hill?
a: Hoarder clean out cost depends on the volume of belongings and how many rooms are affected — a single room prices modestly, a full property costs more given the time required. The exact figure is confirmed free at a private walkthrough, with no premium for a condo tower or a larger estate property.

items.q: Can you handle a hoarding cleanout in our condo without the building making a scene of it?
a: Yes, and that discretion is the whole point. Certificates of insurance go to management at booking, freight elevators reserve ahead, and the work is timed so hallways and common areas see nothing unusual — handled as a routine building visit, not an event.

items.q: What's the best way to clean out a hoarder's house?
a: Professional help, a clear plan, and patience. Going in without a strategy usually causes more distress than progress. The most effective approach sorts systematically — keep, donate, recycle, dispose — respects the resident’s input wherever they’re able to give it, and moves at a pace the household can handle.

items.q: How discreet is a hoarding cleanout on a larger Bayview Hill property?
a: Completely, by design. Arrival times arrange around the family’s schedule, nothing is staged where the road can see it, and no client’s situation is discussed with anyone outside the job.

items.q: How careful are you with heritage homes around Mill Pond?
a: Genuinely careful. Original trim and features that stay get protected, while the sorting inside moves entirely at the family’s own pace.

items.q: Can the cleanout happen while the person continues living in the home?
a: Yes, and it’s one of the most common ways a hoarding cleanout actually happens. Work can proceed room by room while the resident stays in place throughout.

items.q: What happens if we find valuables, documents or sentimental items?
a: They’re set aside immediately and brought to the family or resident, never sorted into a donation or disposal pile by default.

items.q: What if the property has safety hazards — pests, mould, structural damage?
a: Those get flagged honestly. Live Junk Free doesn’t disturb suspected biohazards or structural issues — the concern is identified and the household is pointed toward the right licensed specialist before the rest of the cleanout proceeds.

items.q: Why choose Live Junk Free over a general junk removal company for this?
a: Experience and approach. A hoarding cleanout calls for patience, discretion and a crew that’s done this kind of work often enough to handle it calmly, whatever the property type.
